name: Deep-Forge Coal

rarity.note: A handful of pieces exist; each is a named gift with a recorded lineage.

summary: Lumps of charcoal from the First Forge's original lighting — Orbren's own forge-heat, banked for four thousand years. A piece burns once, underwater if need be, and while it burns no oath spoken beside it can be broken quietly: lies taste of smoke to the speaker. The clans give them rarely, to seal treaties and to arm truth-finders; eleven pieces are recorded, six remain unburned.
origin: ~415 AS — the First Forge's first fire, Hallord
current_whereabouts: Five in clan vaults, one held in trust by the Septuary from a treaty both parties forgot.
properties: Burns once, even submerged — the flame is grey and gives no heat, only light enough to read by
While it burns, lies taste of smoke to the liar; truths taste of nothing
Cannot be extinguished early; it burns until its purpose is spent, which it decides
keepers: The clans; the Septuary's forgotten-trust piece is the only one outside deep-folk hands.
value_or_danger: Not for sale. The clans' question is always 'what will you burn it for', never 'what will you pay'.
adventure_hooks: Players witness a piece burned over a treaty signing — and watch a signatory taste smoke on his own oath.
The Septuary's trust-piece must be returned or claimed before the charter that created it lapses this year.
